fair_value_reason: Using management's 2027-28 average model as the NTM proxy at the Sep-2027 horizon (not 2027 alone, and without adding the 2028 ramp on top): at a $5.90-6.00 deck, EBITDA ~$16.2-16.8B less ~$2.9B D&A/interest, 32% tax, ~39% NCI, 1.444B shares gives EPS ~$3.9-4.0; x16.5x = $64-66. Attributable FCF (OCF ~$12.2-12.5B less $4.8B capex, 61-62% attributable) = ~$3.15-3.25/share at 4.75-5% = $63-68. Removing the half-double-counted 2028 increment trims agents 2, 3 and 5 by ~$1-1.5 each, so the corrected forecaster mean is ~$64.5-65 vs the reported $65.4.

thesis_triggers.event: Around $47 (-33%) the stock discounts sustained copper near $5.25-5.50/lb or a second Grasberg setback / adverse IUPK terms. With the NCI share rising toward ~43% at $5 copper, a true $5 world maps to ~$40-41 (EPS ~$2.7 x 15x), so $47 is already a break of the price leg rather than ordinary 45-48%-vol noise. Agents' range is $46-48; I keep their mean.

supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged: all five agents adopted the round-1 corrections, fair values narrowed to $63-68 (mean $65.4) and the ladders sit within ~0.02 of each other with a median near $69-70, just below the $70.58 spot. The copper-deck ($5.60-6.15) and NCI (~38%, ~$51-54B in EV legs) treatments are now methodologically consistent; the remaining errors are second order: management's $13-20B model is a 2027-28 average (agents 2, 3, 5 double count part of the 2028 ramp), and a constant NCI share understates downside because the 100%-owned US mines are the high-cost assets. The COMEX-stock/tariff risk is adequately in the bear tail and is slower than feared (SMM: re-export is costly), while an enacted tariff would be upside for FCX's COMEX-priced US sales. I make only a small left-tail fattening (confidence low); FCX remains a fairly priced, high-beta copper position with Q3 results ~Oct 22 as the next event.
key_drivers: Copper: spot $6.56/lb is LME-level (front-month COMEX premium gone); management's 2027-28 average model gives ~$13B EBITDA at $5, ~$16.5B at $6, ~$20B at $7 (gold $4,000/oz), so each $0.50/lb is ~$9-10/share and the agents' $5.60-6.15 decks explain their $63-68 fair values

Minority leakage is price-dependent: NCI took 52% of H1 2025 net income at $4.48 Cu (full Grasberg) and 33% of H1 2026 at $6.04 (impaired); US mines (~1.4B lb) are 100% owned, so attributable EPS falls faster than consolidated EBITDA when copper drops
Grasberg ramp: 65% H2-26, ~80% mid-27, near full end-27; 2027 copper sales >20% and gold >50% above 2026, with more growth in 2028
COMEX stock (~770k st) and the undecided Section 232 tariff: a drop is a slow LME drag (re-export costly, ex-US stocks tight); an enacted 15% tariff would lift FCX's COMEX-priced US sales
Valuation: $70.58 is ~17x the $4.16 consensus 2027 EPS; reconciled fair value ~$65, a little below spot
